newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Nov current account deficit $19.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Nov current account deficit $19.3 bln.

text.p: Brazil's January-November current account deficit was $19.333 billion, or 2.83 percent of GDP, up from 2.78 percent in the January-October period, the Central Bank said.
The current account deficit in January-November 1995 was equal to 2.49 percent of GDP, it said.
Net foreign reserves in November stood at $59.233 billion, or $60.471 billion according to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, the bank said.
In October net foreign reserves were $57.325 billion and stood at $58.6 billion under the international liquidity concept, the bank said.
Foreign direct investment to the end of November totalled $7.657 billion, with $942 million being invested in the month of November, the bank said.
The foreign reserve figures presented by the Central Bank matched data provided earlier to reporters by Finance Minister Pedro Malan.
